To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feed restriction and litter application with canola oil reduced the right ventricular hypertrophy and incidence of ascites.
feed restriction reduced the incidence and severity of ascites and litter oiling reduced the severity of ascites in birds fed ad libitum.

1) feed restriction reduced growth rate but reduced mortality from ascites; 2) litter oiling reduced the incidence of respiratory problems in birds that were fed ad libitum but did not reduce the mortality of birds that were feed restricted; and 3) litter oiling in feed-restricted birds reduced the incidence of pulmonary hypertension, a major cause of ascites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of feed restriction and litter treatment on growth performance, ascites incidence, and carcass traits.
the effect of feed restriction in the presence and absence of oiling the litter to reduce respirable dust on broiler performance and carcass traits.
the use of feed restriction and litter oiling to prevent ascites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feed restriction and litter canola oil reduced the incidence of pulmonary hypertension syndrome in broilers.
litter oiling reduced the incidence of respiratory problems, but did not affect the incidence of ascitis.
feed restriction reduces the incidence of ascite, but also reduces gain and litter oiling in feed-restricted groups reduces the incidence of right ventricular hypertrophy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feed restriction is effective for reducing ascites, but litter oiling is not.
litter oiling reduced ascites, but only in ad libitum-fed birds.
feed restriction reduced the incidence, but not the severity of ascites, and litter oiling did not reduce the incidence of ascite in feed-restricted birds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RVA is a useful indicator of the risk of ascites in a broiler flock.
feed restriction is effective at reducing the incidence of ascitis.
litter oiling may reduce ascites in ad libitum fed broilers, but it does not appear to be a viable strategy for feed-restricted birds.
